statement: Half of Leo's toy cars are red. Then he gets 4 more cars, all red. Now he has 10 red cars. How many toy cars does he have now?

choices.misconception: I found how many red cars Leo had at the start and stopped there.
I gave the number of red cars now, not the number of all his cars.
I found how many cars Leo had before he got the new ones.
I thought half of his cars are still red, so I doubled 10.

hints: How many red cars did Leo have before the new ones?
Work backwards: take away the new red cars to find the red cars at the start. Half the cars were red then, which tells you how many cars he had. Then add the new cars back on.
At the start Leo had 10 - 4 = 6 red cars, and that was half of his cars.

solutions.reliable: Before the new cars, Leo had 10 - 4 = 6 red cars. That was half of his cars, so he had 6 + 6 = 12 cars. Then he got 4 more, so now he has 12 + 4 = 16 cars. The idea to keep: a fraction belongs to one moment in the story, so use it only for that moment.
solutions.elegant: The cars that are not red never change. At the start they were the other half, so there are 6 of them, the same as the 6 red cars then. Now he has 10 red cars and 6 other cars: 10 + 6 = 16. The idea to keep: look for the part of the story that stays the same.

whyOnTest: Fractions of a quantity: half was true before the new cars came, and doubling 10 uses the fraction at the wrong moment.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
